the use of microorganisms to regenerate GAC is a feasible process.
the feasibility of using whole‐cell microorganisms to regenerate granular activated carbon was demonstrated.

the bioregeneration process is feasible, and the process parameters that need to be optimized for a successful bioregeneration process include: (1) initial bacterial concentration, (2) bioregeneration time, (3) pore diameter, and (4) carbon surface chemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of whole cell organisms can be an effective means of regenerating spent granular activated carbons loaded with 2‐,4‐D, however, pore size, pore surface recovery, and bioregeneration time all affect the efficiency of bioregeneration.
bioregeneration is a promising alternative to chemical and thermal regeneration methods, and that the use of bacteria as a means of bioregeneration is more efficient than using enzymes.
bioregeneration of activated carbon is possible and that it can be used as an alternative method to chemical regeneration.
